insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: Instant addition of 100% Basic Sum Insured on complete or partial utilization of Your existing Policy Sum Insured and cumulative Bonus (if applicable) during the Policy Year.
great.reference: Section B > II. Other Benefits > 1. Restore benefit (Page 11)
great.explanation: Adds 100% of the Basic Sum Insured instantly when your Sum Insured (and Cumulative Bonus, if any) is partially or fully used during the policy year. This increases available cover for further hospitalisations in the same year.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: On Renewal of this Policy with the Company without a break, a sum equal to 10% of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring Policy shall be provided as Cumulative Bonus irrespective of any claims
great.reference: Section B > III. Renewal Benefits > 2. Cumulative Bonus (Page 16)
great.explanation: Gives a Cumulative Bonus of 10% of Base Sum Insured at renewal even if you made claims. Your cover can keep increasing year-on-year without being reset due to claims.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.reference: Section C > 1(ii) Pre-Existing Diseases: Code - Excl01 (Page 19)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. After 24 months, PED-related claims become payable as per policy terms.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy with us.
good.reference: Section C > 1(i) Specified disease/procedure waiting period: Code - Excl02 (Page 16)
good.explanation: Listed diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months from the policy start date. This is a standard market waiting period you should plan around.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-Hospitalization Medical expenses... incurred upto 30 days before Hospitalisation.
good.reference: Section B > I. Hospitalisation Covers > 2. Pre-Hospitalization Medical expenses (Page 10)
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses incurred up to 30 days before hospitalisation. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post-Hospitalization Medical expenses... incurred upto 60 days after discharge from Hospitalisation.
good.reference: Section B > I. Hospitalisation Covers > 3. Post-Hospitalization Medical expenses (Page 10)
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses incurred up to 60 days after discharge. This supports follow-up visits, diagnostics, and medicines after hospitalisation.

bad.name: Co-pay (Optional)
bad.quote: If opted and mentioned on the Policy Schedule that a Co-payment is effective... the insured person shall bear 20% of the eligible claim amount payable under the Policy
bad.reference: Section D > 2. Specific General Terms > 15. Co-Payment (Page 34)
bad.explanation: If opted and shown on the Policy Schedule, you must pay 20% of each eligible claim amount. This directly increases your out-of-pocket cost on every claim where co-pay applies.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Non-Medical expenses such as Food charges (other than patient’s diet provided by hospital), laundry charges, attendant charges, ambulance collar, ambulance equipment, baby food, baby utility charges and other such items. Full list of Non-Medical expenses is attached
bad.reference: Section C > 3. Specific Exclusions > xii (Page 22) and Annexure I List of Non-Medical Expenses (Page 41)
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items listed (and in the annexure) are excluded from cover. You may have to pay these hospital bill components yourself even when the main treatment is covered.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: In-Patient Treatment... includes: • Hospital room rent or boarding
unclear.reference: Section B > I. Hospitalisation Covers > 1. In-Patient Treatment (Page 9)
unclear.explanation: Hospital room rent/boarding is included under in-patient treatment, but no room category limit or cap is stated in the provided extract. You should confirm from the policy schedule/wording whether any room rent restriction applies, as it can affect claim payouts.

unclear.name: Initial Waiting Period
unclear.quote: All Illnesses and treatments shall be covered subject to the waiting periods specified below:
unclear.explanation: The extract indicates waiting periods apply but does not show the actual initial waiting period duration (commonly 30 days, with accident exceptions). You should check the next lines/clauses in the same section or the schedule to confirm the exact number of days.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
